title: drop-scope-size: confirm size L, plan and team models
body:
drop-scope-size: confirm size L, plan and team models
**Proposed size: L**, `qa-b: yes`, `design: no`, `architecture: no`. Plan: `iterations/1.md`.

Signals:
- Risk flag, breaking contract change: about 200 rules in 17 files under `templates/squad/process/` use `when: size`. Dropping size also breaks the `size:` line in `scope.md`, squad overlays that target size rules, and the tools `squadcompose`, `squadrules`, `squad-spawn`, `squad-start` and `squadreport`. Existing squads need a migration.
- Business questions (the BA owns them, listed in `iterations/1.md`). Examples: which role takes a duty when its usual owner is not in the team; what "done" means once there is no size.
- Order matters: the replacement model first, then the tools, then the rule rewrite, then migration.
- You will see different output: the Manager's team proposal, the `squad-start` and `squad-spawn` output, and `scope.md`.

The brief contradicts two ADRs:
- ADR 0016: the Sizes section and the duty table (SIZE-22).
- ADR 0017 and SIZE-3: "the Manager never proposes the Designer or the Architect."

So the last task (promotion) writes a new ADR that replaces those parts. It also adds removal notes for the dropped rules to `_removed.md`, a changelog entry and a version bump.

Facts:
- This scope runs on plugin 0.5.1, where size still exists. The new behaviour goes into the plugin; this pod keeps working by sizes.
- Version 0.5.1 has no Architect role, so this pod cannot spawn one.
- The open scope `squad-close` also changes this repo. Expect merge conflicts in `templates/squad/process/`.
- Rewriting about 200 rules may not fit in one iteration. If the Tech Lead's design shows that, I will propose splitting it into a goal (option c).

Team models (pin defaults; every role has the advisor on, using Opus):
| Role | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| ba | sonnet | high |
| team-lead | sonnet | medium |
| tech-lead | sonnet | high |
| qa-whitebox | sonnet | high |
| qa-blackbox | sonnet | high |
| dev | sonnet | medium |

To change a row, name the role, model and effort.
options: (a) Confirm L + plan + default models; (b) Confirm with model changes (name rows); (c) Split into a goal (several scopes) instead

reason: PO asked to pick roles per scope; replaced by the team-pick item

title: drop-scope-size: confirm the team picked per role, and its models
body:
drop-scope-size: confirm the team picked per role, and its models
As you asked, I picked each role by what this scope needs, not by its size. The table and the reasons are in `iterations/1.md` → Team.

**In:** BA, Tech Lead, Team Lead, QA whitebox, QA blackbox, Developers (up to 3).
- BA: open business questions (what "done" means without a size, who takes a duty when its usual role is missing, adding a role mid-scope, migration).
- Tech Lead: a breaking contract change (how rules target roles, overlays, tools) and the migration.
- Team Lead: 4 or more tasks in strict order, with Developers working in parallel.
- QA blackbox: you will see different output (the Manager's team proposal, `squad-start` and `squad-spawn` output, `scope.md`).

**Out:**
- Designer: no screen changes. The output is CLI text and markdown, and the HTML report does not show size.
- Architect (recommended out): the role fits this work, a redesign that cuts across the whole system. But this scope runs on plugin 0.5.1, which has no Architect role. Adding one means re-pinning this scope to 0.5.2 (main 2949573) and restarting me. The Architect role was merged today and has never run in a live scope, and this scope rewrites those same rules. Instead, the Tech Lead writes the design for the new targeting model first, before the plan.

**Note:** 0.5.1 still builds its rules from the size. The team I picked has the same roles as size L, so `size: L` stays in `scope.md` only as the key that selects the rules.

Models (0.5.1 defaults, advisor on, using Opus): ba sonnet high, team-lead sonnet medium, tech-lead sonnet high, qa-whitebox sonnet high, qa-blackbox sonnet high, dev sonnet medium. With (b), the Architect uses 0.5.2's default.
options: (a) Confirm the team without an Architect, default models; (b) Re-pin this scope to 0.5.2 and add an Architect; (c) Confirm with model changes (name the rows)

title: drop-scope-size: two team-rule choices (BA proposals)
body:
drop-scope-size: two team-rule choices (BA proposals)
The BA needs two PO decisions for the spec (`tasks/spec.md`, rules 3 and 5). It goes on with its proposals meanwhile.

**P1. Adding Designer or Architect mid-scope.** May the Manager add one on its own?
- Proposed: no, the PO confirms first. They hold up the plan and can reopen built work. Other roles: the Manager adds them alone and reports at the check-in.

**P2. Team shapes.** Allow any team shape (e.g. Team Lead without Tech Lead, QA blackbox without QA whitebox)?
- Proposed: yes. Duty fallback chains cover every shape (all 128 tested) and the Manager's suggestion rules keep odd shapes rare.
- Alternative: a few "X requires Y" rules.

**Decided by the BA without you (tell me to reverse any):** the PO confirms the team; open scopes keep their plugin pin; goal-trigger wording; Token Coach is suggested when a QA is on the team.
options: (a) Accept both; (b) P1 yes, Manager may add Designer/Architect alone; (c) P2 no, add 'X requires Y' rules; (d) other: say which

title: drop-scope-size: confirm the architecture choices I1 to I7
body:
drop-scope-size: confirm the architecture choices I1 to I7
The Architect finished `architecture.md` (Status: final). Seven choices change formats that other scopes and overlays carry, so you decide them. Details: `architecture.md` section 8. I8 is the BA's P2 from the earlier item, so answer it there.

- **I1. Targeting model:** rules key on role presence plus a derived duty owner from one fallback table. Rejected: presence only (too many combinations) and S/M/L renamed as presets.
- **I2. `scope.md`:** one `team:` line replaces `size:`, `design:`, `architecture:` and `qa-b:`.
- **I3. `when:` keys:** `design`, `architecture` and `qa-b` stay as keys, now derived from the team. New keys: `ba`, `team-lead`, `tech-lead`, `qa-whitebox`. About 60 rules and the overlays using them need no edit.
- **I4. Old squads on the new engine:** a read-side shim from `size:` plus a converter. Open legacy scopes keep working. The shim is removed in a later version.
- **I5. Presets:** S/M/L do not survive as named presets.
- **I6. Release:** plugin 0.6.0, breaking. `size` is rejected in `when:`. ADR 0018 supersedes ADR 0016's Sizes and duty table, and amends ADR 0017.
- **I7. New `squad-team` tool:** shows and changes the team and lists the roles to respawn.

Scopes already pinned to an older plugin version are untouched. The Architect recommends the first option on every row.
options: (a) Accept all recommendations; (b) Accept with changes (name the I-numbers and options)

title: drop-scope-size: QA blackbox cannot read its scope files (permission deny)
body:
drop-scope-size: QA blackbox cannot read its scope files (permission deny)
QA blackbox's settings (`roles/plugin-qab-drop-scope-size.settings.json`) deny `Read(//home/chieule/workspace/squad/**)`. This scope's folder is inside that path, so it cannot read `scope.md`, `tasks/spec.md`, its own rules, or later the tickets and `evidence/`. QA whitebox's settings have no such deny.

- I will not change anyone's permissions. Meanwhile the BA sends the business AC by message, so the AC agreement (REV-8) goes on.
- This looks like a plugin defect: the "stay blind to code" deny covers the whole repo, including the scope folder when it lives in the repo. I will draft it as a plugin proposal at the check-in.
- If you pick (b), the allow rule must cover `.claude/squads/plugin/scopes/drop-scope-size/**` and `project.md` only, not code.
options: (a) Keep deny; BA sends QA blackbox the AC by message (QA stays blind to code); (b) You allow Read on the scope folder for QA blackbox (your edit of its settings)
blocks: QA blackbox reading plan, ticket and evidence files

title: drop-scope-size: committing the 15 files makes the merge conflict on 9
body:
drop-scope-size: committing the 15 files makes the merge conflict on 9
I tested "commit them, then merge" in a throwaway worktree (nothing touched in your root). Result: add/add conflicts in 9 ticket files (02, 03, 07, 08, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14). 6 files are identical to the branch and merge cleanly.

Both sides differ: the root copies carry the Team Lead's later notes (for example ticket 13's "Added by Team Lead"), the branch copies carry the Developers' lint and evidence lines. I never resolve a conflict myself, so under (a) the merge would stop at 9 files.

- (a) Commit all 15, then I merge and abort when it conflicts; you resolve the 9.
- (b) Commit only the 6 identical; the branch's 9 versions win. The Team Lead notes in the root copies stay only in `tasks/root-untracked-backup/`.
- (c) Discard the 15 root copies and merge; same outcome as (b) for the history, nothing extra committed to main. Backup is in `tasks/root-untracked-backup/`. You must say so, since a delete in your root was blocked earlier.

The tickets are done work, so the branch versions are the record. Nothing is merged yet.
options: (a) commit all 15 on main, then I merge and abort on the 9 conflicts for you to resolve; (b) commit only the 6 identical files, take the branch's version of the other 9; (c) discard the 15 root copies (backup kept), then merge
